title: Cloud onboarding corpus node
description: One deployable path for getting a cloud log source into Abstract. A node is the unit that generates a Notion page, a builder-app screen, FAQ entries and troubleshooting rows. Everything downstream is generated from these — never hand-edit the generated surfaces.

id.description: Stable primary key, e.g. azure.event-hub.activity-log. NEVER change it once synced — the Notion registry maps it to a page ID.

service.description: The cloud service or log source in the vendor's own words, e.g. 'Azure Monitor Activity Log', 'AWS CloudTrail', 'Cloud Audit Logs'.

direction.description: source = cloud -> Abstract. destination = Abstract -> cloud.

transport.description: How bytes physically move. Distinct from the authoring tool — see artifacts[].kind.

abstract_integration.description: The Abstract-side integration this node feeds. Verified against GET /v1/integrations/.

scopes.description: Deployment scopes this path can bind to. The org-level scope is what makes a path cover future accounts.

covers_future_accounts.description: TRUE only if new accounts/subscriptions/projects created later are onboarded with NO further action. This is the single most-asked customer question — do not set it true without naming the mechanism in mechanism_note.

status.description: gap = Abstract has no integration for this; the node documents the path forward and MUST carry a feature_request.

provenance.description: Tier of the RECOMMENDED artifact — the path we actually tell customers to use. CI enforces the match. Every artifact also renders its own tier, so a weaker convenience snippet alongside a validated template neither inflates nor deflates this.

alternatives_rejected.description: Named and reasoned, so the option is not re-proposed six months later.

decision.description: The choose-your-own-adventure questions. THIS IS THE IP — templates are commodity, the discriminating questions are not. Every question must be answerable by the customer before they touch a console.

ask_who.description: Which human holds this answer — cloud admin, security, network, finance. Onboardings stall when nobody identified this person.

leads_to.description: A node id, an artifact kind, or 'stop:<reason>'.

identity.description: Roles/permissions needed, and AT WHAT SCOPE. The scope mismatch (person has project rights but the action needs org rights) is the #1 onboarding blocker across all clouds.

settings.description: Things that must be switched on first and are off by default (e.g. GCP Data Access audit logs, M365 unified audit log).

lead_time.description: Anything with a propagation delay, e.g. '24-48h for M365 audit log'.

console_walkthrough.description: Click-path for operators who will not touch a CLI. Every node needs one — the GUI is how most customers actually do it the first time.

image.description: Visual for this step. The licence terms below are not decoration: they are what makes the image usable. Microsoft permits screenshots of its software in documentation only if they are UNALTERED except for resizing, are not cropped to a portion, contain no third-party content and no identifiable individual, and carry the credit 'Used with permission from Microsoft'. Google excludes images from the CC-BY licence covering its documentation text entirely. So: prefer 'own-capture' (our terminal, our createUiDefinition form) and 'drawio' over any vendor screenshot.

alt.description: Real alt text. The step is unreadable without it for screen readers and when the image fails to load.

source.description: vendor-doc images are almost never licensed for reuse. vendor-console means we captured the vendor's product ourselves.

credit.description: Verbatim attribution string required by the licence.

tenant_safe.description: True only if the frame shows no tenant, subscription, project, directory or account name, and no person.

altered.description: Must be false for any vendor-sourced image. Resizing is not alteration; cropping, blurring and de-branding are.

delivery_surfaces.description: How the artifact is DELIVERED, which is a different axis from how it is AUTHORED. Octopus/Harness/GitHub Actions orchestrate Terraform or CFN; they are not IaC languages.

verification.description: Ordered checks proving it works, each isolating ONE layer so a failure localises. Cloud-side first, Abstract-side last.

silent.description:
TRUE only when the failure produces ZERO EVENTS AND NO ERROR SIGNAL ANYWHERE -- nothing red, nothing logged, nothing reported non-compliant. These cost days because everyone assumes the pipeline is fine, so they render first.

NOT silent, however expensive: a WRONG or PARTIAL result that is discoverable by looking at one event; a state the platform itself reports (non-compliant, 'Insufficient data', a metric sitting at zero); a cost surprise visible on the bill; or expected latency that is not a failure at all.

The flag only earns its position if it stays a minority. It was over-applied to 29 of 52 entries on 2026-08-26, at which point sorting by it stopped discriminating; the gate now warns above 50%.

seen_on.description: Engagement or date where this was actually observed. Empty = theoretical.

surprise_line.description: The cost nobody budgets for (NAT gateway per-GB, Data Access log amplification, retained cold storage).

detections_unlocked.description: Why a SOC should care. Keeps the corpus from becoming a pile of plumbing docs.

reviews.description: Multi-perspective review. Each lens is written by (or synthesised from) a reviewer pass; empty string means not yet reviewed.

asked_by.description: Real customer/engagement if this came from a live question.

tier.description: vendor-doc outranks everything. community (Medium/blog/forum) is usable but must never be the ONLY support for a factual claim.

supports.description: Which specific claim in this node this reference backs.

supersedes_notion.description: Notion page IDs this node replaces. Drives the consolidation report and the archive pass.

merges_notion.description: Notion page IDs whose content was folded in (credit preserved, page kept).

provenanceTier.description: deployed = executed against a real account. planned = terraform plan / az what-if / CFN changeset against real credentials. validated = compiler or linter passed locally (bicep build, cfn-lint, terraform validate). schema-reviewed = written to the current provider schema but never executed. cited = reproduced from a named vendor doc. NOTHING ships without one, and the tier is rendered on every generated surface.

kind.description: How the artifact is AUTHORED. StackSets and changesets are CloudFormation FEATURES, kept here only because they are separately deployable units.

path.description: Repo-relative path if the artifact is a file in this repo.

external_path.description: Absolute path if it lives in another repo — the canonical copy, per the consolidation audit.

inline.description: The artifact itself, for short snippets embedded directly in the generated page.

validation.description: Evidence. If provenance is validated/planned/deployed this MUST be present and MUST record a command that was actually run.

destructive_risk.description: What this overwrites or replaces. Read-merge-write beats blind write; say which this does.

recommended.description: Exactly ONE artifact per node must set this. It is the path we tell customers to use, and node.provenance must equal ITS tier — so the headline claim tracks the recommended path rather than being dragged down by a convenience snippet or inflated by the best-evidenced one.
